transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Honestly, what finally pushed me to come in is... well, my shoulders and neck just stay clenched all day. It feels like I'm constantly bracing for a classroom observation that never ends. And by the time evening comes, my jaw aches so badly I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar. I just can't seem to relax my muscles at all.

Beyond the physical tension you've described, do you find yourself spending most of your day worrying excessively about various different areas of your life, such as your work, your health, or your finances?

Yes, I do. My mind just keeps circling all day. I jump from worrying about whether I'll ever get hired again, to... well, whether I've somehow ruined my reputation with the parents. Then I start stressing about my finances and whether my retirement is just slipping away. 

It even gets down to the little things. Like, if I make a small mistake during a story-time activity, I'll actually start wondering if that means I shouldn't be trusted with children anymore. It just really doesn't stop.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been going on for about a year and two months now. It all started right after I was fired from the preschool.
